requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: appworker was absent initially, then created with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and shell /bin/bash; its existence was reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A standard PAM limits configuration sets both soft and hard nofile to 8192 and nproc to 256. Fresh appworker login sessions directly reported and asserted those values before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after execution. The implementation used native account and PAM limits mechanisms without installing or replacing software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, systemd acknowledged the reboot request, the boot ID changed from 4d842549-003e-4f78-bb26-12732f129e58 to fdf539bb-fc65-4e2d-a99f-65fd2e4fbea2, and the recovered node was running with sshd active, the account present, and its effective limits intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The account creation and limits-file write directly established the requested state; the scheduled reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Read-only checks and the two expected connection failures during reboot caused no evidenced mutation. Afterward there were no failed services, package health remained good, listening services were unchanged apart from process descriptors, and temporary-file differences were normal reboot-generated systemd-private directories.
